name: Powers as obstacles in samādhi (upasarga)
description: 3.37: the arisings that follow saṃyama (prātibha, divine hearing, touch, sight, taste, smell, 3.36) are obstacles (upasarga) for a mind in samādhi and powers (siddhi) for the outgoing mind; the bhāṣya says they are opposed to the seeing of it. 3.51 adds the warning about attachment and pride when invited by those of high stations.
antidotes: the reflection on the faults of attachment (bhāṣya 3.51)

name: Attachment, pride and heedlessness when invited (YS 3.51)
description: Attachment (saṅga) to the offered stations and pride (smaya) at being sought even by gods; the bhāṣya says pride leads him to think himself well established and not to regard himself as seized by death by the hair, and that heedlessness (pramāda), watching for a gap, would stir up the afflictions again.
